description: Run the sweep over this solet's finished work folders. It reads the work-folder records and acts only on folders whose record says they are finished: a harvested folder is removed from disk and recorded deleted; a closed (due) regenerable folder is first marked harvested, because it keeps nothing; a closed folder that is not regenerable waits, reported in advisories, until a harvest receipt is recorded. It never looks for folders on disk and never decides by age. Before acting on a folder it checks again that the path is still the real directory that was opened (same dev and ino, not a symlink): a folder that fails the check is skipped with an advisory and never deleted, an absent path is recorded as deleted, and a removal that fails is recorded and tried again on the next run. apply False, the default, is a dry run that lists what would happen and writes nothing; apply True removes. At most limit folders (default 200) are acted on per run and the rest are listed in deferred. folder_id, when given, limits the run to that one record, with every check above applied to it: a finished folder is handled, the id of a folder that is not finished (open, retired or already deleted) gives no candidates, and an id with no record is refused unknown_folder. A creator that has just closed its own folder without a receipt uses this to have the solet remove that one folder in the same step. An applying run on a Python whose rmtree cannot avoid symlink attacks stops with aborted True and removes nothing.
embedding_description: Sweep finished scratch folders: a dry run lists which work folders are due for removal, and an apply run deletes the harvested ones and records each removal. Skips anything without a harvest receipt or whose directory changed, and reports why.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Object with candidates (list of entries with folder_id, path, state, action and outcome: action is remove, record_absent, harvest_and_remove or harvest_and_record_absent; outcome is would_ plus the action in a dry run, or deleted, absent, skipped or failed after an apply), counts (marked_harvested, deleted, absent, skipped, failed), deferred (list of folder ids beyond the limit), advisories (list with code, message and, for one folder, folder_id and path) and aborted (bool).
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: For a dry run say how many folders would be removed and list their paths; for an apply say how many were deleted, absent, skipped and failed. Always report advisories by code, and say plainly when aborted is true or deferred is not empty.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: A dry run changes nothing; repeat with apply true to remove. If deferred is not empty, run again to take the rest. A folder named in advisories is kept on purpose: record its missing harvest receipt with transition_work_folder, or retire it, instead of deleting it by hand.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Reading the work-folder records and removing the finished folders through the state service
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: invalid_field: limit is below 1. unknown_folder: no record has that folder_id, so nothing was listed or removed. state_service_unavailable: the state service is not bound, so nothing was listed or removed. A skipped folder, a failed removal or an aborted run is not an error: it is reported in advisories and counts. The code is in data.error_code and prefixes the error text.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For invalid_field, pass a limit of at least 1. For unknown_folder, find the right folder_id with read_work_folders mode list, or leave folder_id out to sweep every finished folder. For state_service_unavailable, wait for the solet to finish starting and retry once. For a removal_failed advisory, read its message, fix what blocks the removal and run the sweep again; the folder stays harvested until it is removed.
